newsitem.title: USA: Koch, Ashland say no run cuts during IPL outage.
newsitem.headline: Koch, Ashland say no run cuts during IPL outage.

text.p: Koch Oil Co and Ashland Inc did not have to cut back refinery throughput at their Minnesota facilities in the wake of the outage Interprovincial Pipe Line earlier this week, officials at both companies said.

The 1.4 million barrel per day (bpd) pipeline system, run by IPL Energy Inc, lost as much as a million bpd of its througput Saturday due to a freak storm that cut power to certain pumping stations. It was fully restored Thursday.
"We had said at the outset that we would operate out of inventories and that has worked out," said Riff Yaeger, a spokesman at Koch Oil, a unit of Koch Industries.
"Fortunately it appears as if they're coming back up today," Yaeger said, referring to IPL's operations.
Koch operates operates a 286,000 barrel per day (bpd) refinery in Rosemount, Minnesota while Ashland runs a 69,000 bpd facility in St Paul Park.
"We've been monitoring the situation but our operations remain unaffected," said Stan Lampe, spokesman at Ashland.
Still some industry sources said Koch, whose refinery is considerably larger than Ashland's, might have been forced to cut their runs.
That suspicion could not, however, be confirmed.
